subject: Next steps & risk matrix: Private hosting requirements for Convergent Health
messages:
From: Mateo Ruiz <mateo.ruiz@convergenthealth.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 14:10:00 -0800
Subject: Private hosting constraints and initial diagram (Convergent Health)

Thanks for the call earlier — good to meet everyone. Per the discovery with our infra and compliance teams, I wanted to capture the primary constraints so we can align on a technical plan: 

- Regulatory driver: PHI in scope; customer requires an air-gapped option for the clinical analytics environment (no outbound internet egress allowed).
- Residency: Data must remain within our US VPC and block any cross-region backups without explicit approval.
- Key management: Keys must be customer-controlled (KMS/HSM) and key usage audit logs must be available for export.
- Logging/retention: We need at least 365 days of immutable audit logs for model inference requests.
- Network: VPC peering allowed but no NAT gateway to public internet. Bastion / jump host for support is acceptable if we sign off on access windows.

Attached: Convergent_Network_Diagram_v1.pdf (shows environments and where we would host models).

Immediate asks from our side:
1) Can Redwood provide a concrete evidence pack for SOC2 + data flow handling (high level is fine for now)?
2) Confirm whether Redwood’s KV cache can be configured to avoid persistent storage of any PII and whether cache can be disabled for a workload.
3) Proposed timeline: we’d like a 2–3 week POC window where we validate networking and a small inference workload.

Please reply with a short plan (one pager) and the names of folks we should include for the technical deep dive (network, security, platform).

— Mateo
Mateo Ruiz
Infra Lead, Convergent Health
mateo.ruiz@convergenthealth.com

From: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Ruiz <mateo.ruiz@convergenthealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Private hosting constraints and initial diagram (Convergent Health)

Thanks Mateo — captured and appreciate the clarity. Summary from Redwood side and a proposed recipe to get the POC moving: 

Redwood summary (short):
- We can support a VPC-hosted private deployment with no outbound internet egress. Dedicated capacity (isolated GPUs) is the recommended path for predictable latency and auditability.
- KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations and can integrate with external HSMs; audit events for key usage are exportable.
- Caching: KV cache is optional per deployment. For PHI workloads we commonly disable persistent KV caching and run inference with strict in-memory-only options and ephemeral cleanup.
- Logging: we can stream audit logs to your log sink (S3/CloudWatch) with retention controls; we will add immutable retention based on your retention policy during provisioning.

Proposed immediate deliverables (for your 2–3 week POC):
1) Technical canary plan (what we run during POC) — attached: redwood-vpc-checklist.xlsx
2) Evidence pack (SOC2 summary + configuration notes) — attached: soc2-assertion-summary.pdf
3) Network checklist / required firewall rules and jump-host access windows (first-pass in checklist).

Next steps / asks for Convergent team:
- Confirm stakeholders for the deep dive (network, security, procurement).
- Confirm whether you can provide a dedicated test VPC / infra contact and a temporary bastion account for the POC.
- Are there specific egress exceptions for package downloads during provisioning? If not, we will use an air-gapped provisioning bundle delivered via secure transfer.

Schedule availability: Ben (solutions) and I can run a 60–75m technical deep dive on Mon/Tue next week (PST mornings). Please confirm times that work.

I’ll follow up with a one-page plan and the risk matrix for the POC.

Best,

Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0196
From: Nora Singh <nora.singh@convergenthealth.com>
To: tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Mateo Ruiz <mateo.ruiz@convergenthealth.com>
Cc: procurement@convergenthealth.com
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarifying retention and PII handling questions

Tessa / Mateo — quick follow-up from compliance after reviewing the attachments:

- Retention: We need a confirmation of exact retention windows for (a) inference request logs, (b) input payloads, and (c) model-generated outputs. Our baseline is 365 days for logs and 90 days for payloads unless otherwise approved.
- PII/PHI in caching: If cache is disabled, will any inference-related PII be written to disk in the hosting environment (tempfiles, swap, overflow)? We need an engineering note describing how you guarantee in-memory-only processing if cache is disabled.
- Evidence: Please include the hash for the SOC2 summary or pointer to the signed assertion (we cannot accept unsigned summaries).

Attached: convergent-questions.docx (details and a few sample legal questions).

Can you provide concise answers so we can include them in our procurement packet?

Thanks,
Nora
Director, Compliance — Convergent Health
From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Nora Singh <nora.singh@convergenthealth.com>, tessa_morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Mateo Ruiz <mateo.ruiz@convergenthealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 6 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarifying retention and PII handling questions

Nora — thanks for the clear list. Short answers here, we’ll follow up with an engineering note and a signed SOC2 assertion link by EOD Monday: 

- Retention: Logs (inference request metadata + audit events) = configurable; default will be set to 365 days for the POC and we can extend per your retention policy. Input payloads = configurable; for the POC we recommend 90-day retention unless you require immediate truncation. Model outputs = policy-controlled; can be configured to 0 days (no persistent storage) for sensitive runs.
- PII in disk: With cache disabled we operate with:
  * zero persistent KV write paths enabled
  * inference artifacts processed in-memory and flushed to ephemeral tmpfs mounts that are mounted with no-swap and removed on container shutdown
  * we will provide a short runbook describing the tmpfs+no-swap configuration and process teardown to meet your audit ask.
- SOC2 evidence: PM will provide a signed assertion (DocID) and we will include a hash and verifier link.

Ben notes (technical): For the POC we propose a canary that runs 50–100 inference requests/hour across a small model, with network capture limited to metadata only. We’ll request read-only CloudWatch/S3 access to validate logging delivery (timeboxed).

Action items (Redwood):
- Ben: provide engineering runbook (tmpfs + cache config) — target: Mon EOD
- Tessa: share proposed deep-dive slots and final POC checklist (attached earlier)
- Convergent: confirm procurement lead and infra contact for the 2–3 week POC

Attachments referenced: redwood-vpc-checklist.xlsx, soc2-assertion-summary.pdf

— Ben Carter
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
